title: What Timezone Am I In? Zone, Offset and Time
description: Answer 'What Timezone Am I In?' from your point — IANA zone name, UTC offset and current local time, by click or GPS. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a traveller waking in a border motel reads America/Chicago, UTC−5, daylight saving in force — three facts that rebuild the day's schedule in one glance.
quick_answer: What Timezone Am I In? shows the timezone name, UTC offset and current local time for your point. Click the map or use GPS and read the zone — the IANA name your calendar and code actually use, with the offset for today and daylight saving's state applied.

body.t: Landed somewhere with the phone confused: the point's zone, offset and local time settle what to set and what to believe. The
rebuilds the home call from it.
A meeting rendered at the wrong hour is usually a zone assumption. This page gives the ground truth for the place in question.
Cabins, rigs and field stations keep zones too. Their IANA names belong in the site file; get them here.
Whether your point is in daylight saving right now — the fact that changes two weekends a year and confuses every static chart.
CST means Chicago, Beijing or Havana depending on the map — the IANA name (America/Chicago) is the unambiguous answer this page leads with.
UTC−6 today can be UTC−5 in July at the same point. The page shows today's, labelled with DST's state — because an offset without a date is half an answer.

faq: Yes — the current daylight-saving state is part of the answer, and the offset shown is today's, DST included where in force.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — click any point instead of GPS; the answer is about the point, not about you.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Zone borders are political and occasionally move; databases vintage differently, so a fresh change can read differently across tools briefly.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — a GPS fix serves the answer and is not kept.
The IANA name is shown because abbreviations collide worldwide (CST, IST, BST all have multiple meanings). The name never collides.
Phones cache carrier and settings quirks; the point's zone from the database is the reference. Check the phone's automatic-zone setting next.
Maritime zones answer (Etc/GMT bands and the like) — a zone exists even where no one sets a table by it.
Both resolve per point — county-level Eastern/Central splits and Arizona's DST abstention are the database's home territory.
Historical zone for an old timestamp?
Rules carry history in the database; this page's headline is the present. Timestamp converters on this site handle dated instants.
